<!--
Write for the reviewer, not as release notes. Start with why the change exists,
then explain the behavior or design that changed.

Use as much detail as the change needs: one sentence may be enough for a small
fix; a cross-cutting change should explain causality, tradeoffs, migration
impact and known limitations. Use headings or bullets only when they make a
long description easier to review.

Do not enumerate files, commits or every feature in the diff. Do not repeat CI
checks visible on the PR. Mention a test, benchmark, manual check or untested
area only when it gives the reviewer useful evidence. Link the issue, ADR or
prior PR when it supplies context.

The author owns every claim. Verify the draft and rewrite it in your own voice.

Delete this comment before submitting.
-->
